events.text: You are the oldest on the bench now. The others are dead, or gone to their families, and the new ones are young to you, sixty and seventy. They have asked you to say, as the oldest always does, what you have learned.

choices.text: Say: the world is better than it looks

effects.log: You say the world is better than it looks, and its people are better than they think. The young elders nod. You have reason to know.

choices.text: Say: nobody knows anything, and that is fine

effects.log: You say nobody knows anything, really, and that is the best part. The bench laughs, and agrees, and you all sit in the sun.

choices.text: Say: be kind to whoever made all this

effects.log: You say: whoever made all this was trying their best. The bench looks at you oddly. You do not explain. It is the most you have ever said about it.

events.text: The people of {pw_world} disagree, as people do, about what comes after death. The priests say the dead go to the god. The farmers say they go into the earth and come back as wheat. Children say they become stars. A young priest, sent to comfort the old, has come to ask you what you think.

choices.text: Say: to the god

effects.log: You say they go to the god. The young priest is relieved. You do not say that you were the god, once, and do not remember anyone arriving.

choices.text: Say: back into the world

effects.log: You say they go back into the world: wheat, rain, stars, children. The young priest is troubled and writes it down anyway.

choices.text: Say: nobody knows, and you are curious

effects.log: You say you do not know, and that you are curious to find out. The young priest has never met an old person who was curious about it before.

events.text: The young priest comes back every week now, to sit with you under the tree by the temple. Tonight the priest is upset: a child of the village has died of fever, and the parents asked the priest where the child has gone, and the priest did not know what to say.

choices.text: Tell the priest what you would say

effects.log: You say: tell them the child is held. By whom, you do not say. The priest goes back, and says it, and the parents are comforted.

choices.text: Go with the priest to the parents

effects.log: You go with the priest, an old person and a young one, to sit with the parents. You say nothing for an hour. It is the right thing.

choices.text: Tell the priest it is all right not to know

effects.log: You tell the priest that not knowing is honest, and the parents will know it. The priest goes back and says: I do not know, but I am here. It helps.

events.text: Your last season, you suspect. The young priest is not so young now, and sits with you under the tree, and asks the question at last: are you afraid?

choices.text: Say no

effects.log: You say no, and mean it. You have been the end of a world and the beginning of one. You are only curious, and a little tired.

choices.text: Say a little, and that it is all right

effects.log: You say a little, and that it is all right, because everyone who ever lived here was a little afraid, and went anyway. The priest holds your hand.

choices.text: Say you will come back and tell the priest

effects.log: You say you will come back and tell the priest what it is like. The priest laughs and cries at once. On quiet nights, for years after, the priest waits under the tree.

events.text: In {pw_world} the old choose how they will be laid to rest, and the choosing is a small festival: friends gather, the priest comes, and the old person says it out loud, so that nobody can argue later. Your friends have gathered, with cakes. They are waiting.

choices.text: Say: the old way of this land

effects.log: You say you want the old way of {pw_land}, the way everyone here has always gone. The friends are moved. The priest writes it down with a little bow.

choices.text: Say: under the temple of the god

effects.log: You ask to lie under the god's temple floor, which is an honour hardly anyone asks for. The priest blinks, and agrees. You do not explain why it seems only fair.

choices.text: Say: somewhere with a view, and no fuss

effects.log: You say a hill with a view, and no fuss, and a good party. The friends cheer. The party is planned in more detail than the burial.

events.text: The temple has sent a stonecutter to ask what you want carved over your resting place. Most people choose a line from the god's record, or their name and a blessing.

choices.text: Carve: here lies someone who made things

effects.log: Here lies someone who made things. The stonecutter carves it, and asks what things. You say: oh, everything. The stonecutter laughs.

choices.text: Carve: thank you

effects.log: Just: thank you. The stonecutter says that is the best one anyone has asked for. Thank you to whom? To all of it, you say.

choices.text: Carve nothing at all

effects.log: You ask for a plain stone. Let them guess. The stonecutter, who has carved a thousand names, says it is a relief.

choices.text: Carve: I came back to see

effects.log: I came back to see. The priests do not know what to make of it. A hundred years later, pilgrims come to read it.

events.text: A last walk, on a fine day, through the town you have lived in: the market, the temple, the old places of your life in this world. People come out of their doors to greet you.

choices.text: Stop and talk to everyone

effects.log: You talk to everyone. It takes all day. By evening you have said goodbye to the whole town without once using the word.

choices.text: Walk to the temple and sit

effects.log: You sit in the god's temple until dusk, watching the light move across the statue's face. It is a good face. You did well, more or less.

choices.text: Walk out of town to the hills

effects.log: You walk out to the hills and look back at all of it: roofs, smoke, fields, the temple, the sky. You made this, once. It made you, this time. That seems fair.

events.text: On winter nights in {pw_world} the old tell the young the story of the world: how the god made it, and {pw_record}, and how the first people came. Every teller tells it differently. The children of the street have gathered at your fire, and are demanding it from you.

choices.text: Tell it as the priests tell it

effects.log: You tell it as the priests do, carefully, every word. The children are good and quiet. One of them falls asleep. You tuck a blanket round the child.

choices.text: Tell it as you remember it

effects.log: You tell it as you remember it, which is not quite how the priests tell it: funnier, lonelier, with more mistakes. The children are spellbound. They come back every night.

choices.text: Make the children tell it to you

effects.log: You make them tell it. Their version has a dragon in it, and a very big sandwich. You think it is an improvement.

events.text: The children have grown, some of them, and tell your version of the story to their own little ones, and the priests have heard of it. A priest comes to your fire, stern, to hear the heresy for themselves.

choices.text: Tell it to the priest, all of it

effects.log: You tell it. The priest listens with folded arms, then unfolded, then with a hand over the mouth. At the end the priest says: where did you hear that? You say: I was there.

choices.text: Tell the priest's version, to be polite

effects.log: You tell the priest's version, word perfect. The children, outraged, correct you all the way through. The priest gives up and laughs.

choices.text: Ask the priest to tell it instead

effects.log: The priest tells it, a little stiffly. You ask questions. By the end, the priest is telling it better, and the children love it.

events.text: The last telling. You are very tired, and the fire is small, and the children around it are new ones, and the old ones, grown, stand at the back. Everyone knows. Nobody says.

choices.text: Tell the end of the story

effects.log: You tell the end, the one you never told: that the god came back, to live as a person, to see what it was like. The fire crackles. The children ask if the god liked it. You say: very much.

choices.text: Tell it short, and let them finish it

effects.log: You tell the beginning and stop, and the children finish it, all together, in your words. You close your eyes and listen to your own story told by others.

choices.text: Tell them it is their story now

effects.log: You say: it is your story now, change it. They look at each other. Somewhere in the back, someone starts a new version, with a dragon in it.
